source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: Ousmane Dieng
injuries.short_comment: Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports.
injuries.long_comment: Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

injuries.name: Dean Wade
injuries.short_comment: Wade (hamstring) won't play Saturday against the Bucks.
injuries.long_comment: Wade was able to get through a full practice Friday, but the 76ers' medical staff still isn't quite ready to clear him for game-time action. His next chance to play will come Monday against the Trail Blazers. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker will continue to help pick up the slack while Wade is sidelined.

injuries.name: Jaylen Brown
injuries.short_comment: Brown (hamstring) went through individual work during Friday's practice, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
injuries.long_comment: Brown is set to be re-evaluated this weekend due to a left hamstring strain, meaning his next chance to play will come Monday against Portland. Dean Wade (hamstring), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker are all candidates for increased minutes while Brown is sidelined.

injuries.name: Tyrese Maxey
injuries.short_comment: Maxey (foot) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
injuries.long_comment: Maxey sat out Wednesday's 121-116 win over the Magic, but he was a full participant at Friday's practice, so he's trending in the right direction. If Maxey is cleared to return, Anfernee Simons would likely head back to the second unit and VJ Edgecombe's usage rate would dip.

injuries.name: Dominick Barlow
injuries.short_comment: Barlow (back) is probable for Saturday's game versus the Bucks.
injuries.long_comment: Barlow is on the precipice of making his season debut following a long recovery due to a lower-back stress reaction. With Adem Bona (back) sidelined, Barlow should immediately slot into the No. 2 center spot behind Joel Embiid on Saturday.

injuries.name: Ariel Hukporti
injuries.short_comment: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.long_comment: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

injuries.name: Adem Bona
injuries.short_comment: Bona (back) participated in Friday's practice, though he still needs to go through a full practice with contact before being cleared to return to game action, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports.
injuries.long_comment: Bona hasn't played since Nov. 4 due to a back sprain, though he appears to be trending in the right direction. Until the big man is cleared to play, Dominick Barlow (back) and Jabari Walker are candidates for increased minutes.
